routes.label: Compare each difference with the smaller sale

question:
Northside’s Drum and Bugle Corps raised money for a trip. The drummers and bugle players kept separate sales records. In each pair on the graph, the open bar represents drums and the shaded bar represents bugles. According to the double bar graph of monthly sales below, in what month did one group’s sales exceed the other’s by the greatest percent?

[Figure 1](figures/1992_AMC_8_Q21_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
To find the percent by which the larger sale exceeds the smaller, divide their difference by the smaller sale, then multiply by \(100\%\). A large difference alone does not guarantee a large percentage.

Count the equal blocks in the graph. The drum and bugle sales, respectively, are \((7,9)\) in January, \((5,3)\) in February, \((9,6)\) in March, \((9,12)\) in April, and \((8,10)\) in May. We can use blocks as our unit because the same sales amount per block cancels in each ratio. All the smaller sales are positive, so every division is valid.

The relative excesses are
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{Jan: }&\frac{9-7}{7}=\frac27,\\
\text{Feb: }&\frac{5-3}{3}=\frac23,\\
\text{Mar: }&\frac{9-6}{6}=\frac12,\\
\text{Apr: }&\frac{12-9}{9}=\frac13,\\
\text{May: }&\frac{10-8}{8}=\frac14.
\end{aligned}
\]
Every ratio except February's is at most \(\frac12\), while \(\frac23>\frac12\). Thus February has the greatest excess, namely \(\frac23\times100\%=66\frac23\%\). The answer is \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
